found.recommendation:
Yes. On honest light, fixed-7 can replace live. Live rests on two tricks: the horn card and the shadow-ray shortcut. Fixed-7 has neither. Its render settings are the honest ones, and every light in it is something a bar or a location photographer could have. All 16 lamps and the three softboxes are out of frame and under the ceiling.

Exceptions, none of which changes what the picture shows at the site's sizes:
(1) Code I could not check. The softbox builder, the shortcut cut and the pendant LEDs are not in the folder. shadow_ray_report also runs before the three softboxes are built, so its "0" does not cover them. The picture is consistent with honesty: no cream lightbox glow, a dark cone, and the softbox seen in the pendant shells where geometry puts it.
(2) Rig collisions, by the README's own box model. The near softbox runs up to 16 mm into the ceiling diffuser. track-horn1 and track-bar1 shine into the backs of the softboxes, 93 % and 87.5 % blocked. No edge shows, and the areas they light read the same as live or brighter.
(3) Bodiless engine discs. The track heads sit 5 cm under the ceiling with no cans, and the two big fills block no light. Negligible effect.

Before it goes up, or at the next render: move shadow_ray_report last and keep its line and the "NO GLASS SHADOWS" count with the frame. Dump the ray flags of every emitter, the 72-plus LED lamps included. Drop the near softbox 2 cm. Switch off or move track-horn1 and track-bar1. None of this needs to hold the frame. The dark horn comes from the lights as placed, not from a trick. Whether it reads well is the photo critic's call, not a light-honesty fault.
found.summary:
I read fixed7.json, the README, meas.md and meas6.md, lights.py, render.py, planet_bar.py, and live.json for comparison. I checked every light and emitter against the engine code. I projected every lamp and softbox into the frame with render.py's own camera model; a lens-shift sign error in my first pass is fixed in geom.txt. I traced 4000 rays from each lamp's beam against the softbox bodies, drew sections through the conflicts, and looked at 1x, 2x and lifted crops of fixed-7 beside live.

Fixed-7 has 16 engine area lamps, all DISK and all out of frame (nearest is track-bay0, 54 px above the top edge). It has three mesh softboxes, all out of frame (nearest is the far skirt corner, about 80 px outside the top-left corner) and all under the 3.40 ceiling (2.1, 4.0 and 1.0 cm clear). The practicals in frame are 5 Hemispheres and 3 Cores. There are no panels, flags, glints, light or shadow links, shares or transmission flags. Both caustics are on, clamp is 0 and filter_glossy is 0. The shortcut-cut prop comes after everything that could carry the shortcut. The fills are inside the room.

The issues: the softbox, cut and lamp code are not in the folder; shadow_ray_report runs before the softboxes; the near softbox runs 16 mm into the diffuser; track-horn1 and track-bar1 are almost fully blocked by the softboxes; and the emitters are bare discs with no bodies. None changes the picture visibly.

Live's horn card and shortcut are confirmed in live.json, so fixed-7 should replace live.

Evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b62/critic7-lights/:

verdicts.reasoning:
Every code claim reproduces, line for line, and the site's file is this live frame.

The bell's gold is the card seen through the clear horn. The patch is a trapezoid, the card's shape. In fixed it drops to 0.2 once the card is hidden from transmission rays (the rays that pass through clear parts).

The card is a light no bar or photographer could rig. Only reflections and see-through rays can see it. It gives no diffuse light, casts no shadow and is hidden from the camera. It is ramped, and 38 % of it hangs above the ceiling. Its gold is plain at 1600 px, at 800 px and in the 168 px thumbnail. That makes it blocking for live.

The band's even cream also goes once the tricks are cut: in fixed it falls to 42-51 L* and turns lemon. Fixed changed four things at once. Of those, reflective caustics only add light, filter_glossy is a blur and the drinks are far off. So the drop comes from cutting the shortcut, perhaps helped by hiding the card, which could otherwise reach the batts through the acrylic.

Limits:
- The shortcut's material code and the fixed run's '7 materials' log are not in the folder. Its presence in live rests on README.md, gen.py and this A/B comparison.
- The band's evenness is not impossible in itself. Real light through flat acrylic is barely displaced, and part of fixed's mottling is caustic sampling noise from a 14 cm head. So the band is a look the trick makes, not a visibly false one. This changes nothing: the owner's rules bar the shortcut, and the bell alone is blocking.

verified.recommendation_check:
I would keep the recommendation, with two changes.

What I confirmed with my own evidence:
- Live rests on the card and the shortcut (L1).
- fixed7.json has no horn-card and no panel of any kind. Its render is the honest one: both caustics on, clamp 0, filter_glossy 0. No light has receivers, shadow_on_set, a flag or a glint.
- There are 16 area lamps, and the softboxes are props 21-23. Under the README's box model the softboxes clear the 3.40 ceiling by 3, 21 and 40 mm (rig.txt).
- The prop order is 19 no_glass_shadows, 20 shadow_ray_report, 21-23 softbox. render.py builds the set (lines 146-153) before any lamp (lines 204-208), so the report also runs before all 16 lamps. The lamps carry no materials, so only the softboxes and anything built after them go unchecked.
- Under the same model, the rig collisions reproduce:
  - The near box runs up to 16.1 mm into the ceiling diffuser's 20 mm body.
  - track-horn1 sits 8.2 cm behind the near box's back, inside its outline, and its beam axis hits that back.
  - track-bar1 sits 12.6 cm behind the far box's back.
  - Neither leaves an edge, at 1x or at +2 stops (cores-cloth-live-over-f7-2x.png, ceiling-left-live-over-f7-plus2.png).
- The picture is consistent with the softboxes being visible to every ray that matters here:
  - They show in the pendant shells, so reflections see them.
  - With the shortcut cut, the batts behind the acrylic rose from 42-51 L* in fixed to 57-59 in fixed-7, so light reaches them through clear parts.

Change 1: "the areas they light read the same as live or brighter" is wrong for track-horn1. Its 12-degree spot is the near horn. That reads 0.7 in fixed-7 against 8.9 in live, and live's 8.9 is the card. In fixed, the head is unblocked and there are no softboxes, and the horn reads 0.3. So losing the head costs nothing visible. Say that instead.

Change 2: the emitter flag dump and moving shadow_ray_report last need no render. render.py's --probe path builds the whole scene and returns before rendering (lines 311-330). The build took 99-107 s, against 1673-1806 s of render. Do these two before it goes up, because they are the only honesty checks not yet shown. Dropping the near box 2 cm and dealing with the two blocked heads can wait for the next render.

Add to the case against live: 38 % of the card hangs above the ceiling, and its gold shows in the site's own thumbnail.

Scope: "can replace live" holds on light honesty only. The owner's first rule is looking real, so the replacement still waits on the photo critic's verdict on the dark horn.

found.summary: (a) Fixed-7 reads more like a real photograph.
